title: Gatebraid gate-run record (gatebraid/gate-run@3)
description: Machine-readable record of one gate execution on one Slice, embedded as the fenced yaml block of the gate evidence file (templates/gate0..3-evidence.md). Successor to gatebraid/gate-run@2, which is NOT edited and NOT retro-broken: @2 records stay valid as @2 forever, and every M3 gate record from Slice P2-S7 on is written as @3 (ADR-0037). Deltas from @2, each traceable to a committed source: (1) repair_attempts[].kind discriminates the D6 red-check sequence from a record-correction repair, and friction #94's conditional keys on two red_check attempts without an in-sequence consult rather than on a bare count (ledger 193); (2) approvals[].type gains `Writer Assignment` (ledger 194); (3) top-level `qualifications[]` is the data-layer home for a statement a record could previously carry only in a YAML comment (ledger 194); (4) plan_hash and allowlist_hash carry the 64-hex pattern the Gate 1 contract states; (5) a repair attempt that names a consult_ref requires that consult to appear in consults[] (ledger 238(c)). Everything else is @2 byte for byte in intent; the @2 text of every carried description stands.

environment.description: Carried from @1 unchanged. NOTE the deliberate vocabulary difference from gatebraid/evidence-capture@1's platform.os, which is the OS a single capture actually ran on (windows|wsl|linux|macos): this field is the Project's Environment value for the gate, which additionally admits macos-authority (a role, not an OS) and mixed-see-prose (no single value is true). The join for a dual-platform claim is windows to windows and wsl to wsl; macos-authority maps to capture os macos; mixed-see-prose maps to no single capture by construction and is read from the prose. Recorded here rather than left for a reader to infer, because N3 re-derives verdicts from the JSON and schemas alone.

base_sha.description: @2 delta (ADR-0029 P1-1): the FULL 40-hex object name. @1 admitted 7-40 hex, so a record could name an abbreviation that is unique today and ambiguous after the next thousand objects — a replayability claim the record could not keep.

started_at.description: F1 correct-course (M3 batch N1D, external review). THE PATTERN IS THE ONLY ENFORCEMENT and `format` is REMOVED. `format: date-time` is asserted only when a validator is constructed with a format checker AND an optional package is present; `fixtures/run-corpus.py` constructs none, so this field accepted arbitrary strings. The evidence-capture@1 correct-course closed exactly this class at N1C and the repair was not propagated to the sibling interfaces — the external reviewer caught the omission. WHAT THIS ENFORCES: RFC3339 LEXICAL FORM only, case-insensitive in the separator and zone designator per RFC 5234. FIELD RANGES ARE UNCHECKED — a month of 13 or an offset of +99:99 matches, as does 2026-02-31. Anchored with (?![\s\S]) rather than $, because Python's re matches $ before a final newline while ECMA-262, which JSON Schema specifies, does not. Quote this scalar in YAML. A YAML 1.1 loader resolves an unquoted ISO8601 scalar to a datetime object, which is not type string, and validation fails (friction #55). The loader that validated is recorded beside the record.

ended_at.description: F1 correct-course (M3 batch N1D, external review). THE PATTERN IS THE ONLY ENFORCEMENT and `format` is REMOVED. `format: date-time` is asserted only when a validator is constructed with a format checker AND an optional package is present; `fixtures/run-corpus.py` constructs none, so this field accepted arbitrary strings. The evidence-capture@1 correct-course closed exactly this class at N1C and the repair was not propagated to the sibling interfaces — the external reviewer caught the omission. WHAT THIS ENFORCES: RFC3339 LEXICAL FORM only, case-insensitive in the separator and zone designator per RFC 5234. FIELD RANGES ARE UNCHECKED — a month of 13 or an offset of +99:99 matches, as does 2026-02-31. Anchored with (?![\s\S]) rather than $, because Python's re matches $ before a final newline while ECMA-262, which JSON Schema specifies, does not. Quote this scalar in YAML — see started_at (friction #55).

result.description: passed → Gate field advances. stopped → e.g. dirty baseline at Gate 0 (Next Approval = Dirty Baseline Acceptance).

bootstrap_exception.description: @2 delta (M3-PLAN.md §2, N2/N3 bootstrap boundary). Present and true ONLY on N2's and N3's own gate landings, and only before O0. It records that this gate read startability from an operator-approved closed-set state packet rather than from the snapshot/frontier pair, which fails open on the control plane's input and is therefore not startability authority before O0. A record so marked claims NO N3 independent validation (N2's records are re-validated after N3's own Gate 3) and is EXCLUDED from V's admission series. The exception is one-time and expiring: dead at N2 + N3 Gate 3 completion, and no later Slice may use it. Absence means the ordinary authority applied.

result.description: none_configured (ADR-0019 §1): the thing this check inspects does not exist to be checked — e.g. CI where no workflow is configured. It is a finding, not a pass, and is distinct from skipped (deliberately not run) and not_run (exists, was not executed).

output_ref.description: Where the raw output lives (evidence file section, committed log path). On a bootstrap_exception record this is the pointer to the committed capture file holding the state packet's exact query identities and outputs (M3-PLAN.md §2).

consults.description: Every consult this gate ran, whenever it ran -- in sequence or at the Human Diagnosis stop -- so the array is the roster and consult_ref is the position. repair_attempts[].consult_ref remains scoped to in-sequence consults; an HDR-directed consult appears here and never as a consult_ref (friction #94). @3 makes the in-sequence half enforceable: a consult_ref without a matching roster entry is invalid (ledger 238(c)).

repair_attempts.$comment: F8 correct-course (N1D). GROUNDED: protocols/gate-2-contract.md fixes the D6 repair sequence as 'repair 1 ... Codex consult ... repair 2 ... Human Diagnosis Required' and states `repair_limit = 2`; no third repair (quoted as written, lowercase); the control-plane spec §1 'caps repairs at repair_limit (default 2)'; ADR-0002 §4 fixes the same sequence; templates/slice.md carries `repair_limit: 2`. maxItems enforces the cap, prefixItems fixes the order — the sequence is repair 1 THEN repair 2 — and each position $refs $defs/repairAttempt so the per-attempt constraints keep applying. The first form of this repair set prefixItems beside a sibling `items` and thereby orphaned it; see $defs/repairAttempt.

author.description: @2 delta (ADR-0029 P1-1): structurally REQUIRED. @1 made it optional so evidence predating the identity split kept validating, which meant the schema could not catch its absence — and absence is precisely what friction #71 produced, an approval-shaped comment authored by the executor's own machine account. The value is the login OBSERVED as the comment's author at verification time, not the login expected. It is deliberately NOT constrained to a constant: the gate contracts decide validity (gate-2-contract Entry; ADR-0020 §4 — an approval authored by any account other than the operator's personal one is invalid as if absent), and a schema that admitted only the valid login would make a wrongly-authored observation unrecordable, which is the ADR-0019 failure class this project already fixed once at the check level.

type.description: @2 delta (M3-PLAN.md §2): the last two are new. 'State Packet Approval' is the operator's approval of the closed-set state packet a bootstrap gate reads startability from. 'Host Instruction Baseline Approval' is the operator's approval of the enumerated host instruction files and their SHA-256 baseline (M3-PLAN.md §2, N1's hard precondition). Both exist so that a gate record can show the checks that gated it rather than referring to them from outside. @3 delta (ledger 194): `Writer Assignment` is the operator's act that names the writer for Gate 2; at @2 it could only be typed as a Plan Approval, so two distinct operator acts read as one.

comment_url.description: URL of the recorded human approval comment.

THE PATTERN IS THE ONLY ENFORCEMENT and `format` is REMOVED. `format: date-time` is asserted only when a validator is constructed with a format checker AND an optional package is present; `fixtures/run-corpus.py` constructs none, so this field accepted arbitrary strings. refrozen.description: Present and true when plan_hash carries a re-frozen plan (correct-course step 5). The delta record comment remains the authority for what changed and why; absence means first freeze (friction #50).

plan_hash.description: Gate 1+: hash of the frozen plan. @3: SHA-256, lowercase hex (gate-1-contract).

allowlist_hash.description: Gate 1+: hash of the frozen write allowlist. @3: SHA-256, lowercase hex (gate-1-contract).

hash_commands.description: Gate 1+: the exact commands that reproduce plan_hash and allowlist_hash (ADR-0011 §3). A hash nobody can recompute is decoration.

handoff_fingerprint.description: Gate 2 exit: what Gate 3's drift check compares against (ADR-0011 §2). Git's own content addressing, not a hash of diff text.

stop_record.description: Required whenever result is `stopped` or `blocked`: what failed and where it went (ADR-0013). A gate that stopped must be recordable as stopped; otherwise writing nothing becomes the only honest option.

stopped_at.description: The action that failed, by number and name.

next_approval.description: Decidable dispositions only. Deliberately NOT extended with the two bootstrap approval types: those gate a record's admissibility and are obtained before the gate runs, so neither is ever the approval a stopped gate is waiting on. M3-PLAN.md §2 extends approvals[].type only.

workflow.description: Error dispositions only; pair with a typed needs_input comment.

remediation_attempted.description: Always none. Gates never remediate — the schema enforces it.

allOf.$comment: F4 correct-course (N1D). GROUNDED, both directions, in protocols/gate-0-contract.md's failure-disposition definitions: 'Decidable ... result: stopped; SET THE MATCHING Next Approval' and 'Error ... Workflow = Blocked with a typed needs_input reason'. So a decidable stop must carry next_approval and must not carry workflow. Before this, both field descriptions said 'X dispositions only' and neither was enforced; the external reviewer validated a decidable stop carrying workflow and an error stop carrying next_approval.

F4, the error branch. Same grounding: an error disposition is 'Workflow = Blocked' and has nothing for a human to accept, so next_approval — the field by which a row reaches the human — must be absent.

field.description: The record field the statement qualifies, as a JSON pointer or a field name.

cited.description: The ruling, friction entry or contract clause the qualification rests on.

qualifications.description: @3 delta (ledger 194): the data-layer home for a qualification that at @2 could live only in a YAML comment, which yaml.safe_load does not return. A structure that cannot express the truth states here what it cannot express.

allOf.$comment: friction #94 as @2 carried it, re-keyed at @3 on the sequence its own comment describes (ledger 193): two red_check attempts, neither carrying an in-sequence consult_ref, validate only as human_diagnosis_required. Two record_correction attempts do not trip it. Nothing can force a false consult_ref.

@2 addition. A record claiming the bootstrap exception must carry the approval that authorized it AND the pointers to the captures it read. Without the first, bootstrap_exception is a self-granted permission — the exact self-certification shape ADR-0028 was written against. Without the second, the record can claim the packet was read and point at nothing: M3-PLAN §2's bootstrap-boundary paragraph makes the checks[].output_ref pointer to committed capture files constitutive of the boundary, not decorative.

@2 addition, BEYOND the four deltas ADR-0029 P1-1 and M3-PLAN §2 N1 enumerate — flagged for operator ratification at approval. @1 declared stop_record 'Required whenever result is stopped or blocked' in a description and enforced it with nothing, so a stopped gate could validate while saying nothing about what stopped it. That is the ADR-0013/ADR-0019 failure class: a gate that stopped must be RECORDABLE as stopped. @2 is the last moment to fix it without buying an N1 correct-course later, because M3-PLAN §2 forbids N2 and N3 from redefining a frozen interface during implementation.

@3 delta (ledger 238(c)): a repair attempt naming an in-sequence consult_ref requires consults[] to be non-empty. consults[] enumerates every consult this gate ran, in sequence or at the Human Diagnosis stop; the P2-S5 record carried consults: [] beside a consult_ref, which @2 admitted.

consult_ref.description: consult_id if a Codex consult occurred in sequence — at this attempt's position in the unified repair sequence. A consult performed at the Human Diagnosis stop is recorded in top-level consults, never here (friction #94).

kind.description: @3 delta (ledger 193): which sequence this attempt belongs to. `red_check` is the D6 repair sequence of gate-2-contract (a review or check red, a repair with a new hypothesis); `record_correction` is a repair to the record itself under route A. Only red_check attempts count toward friction #94's conditional and toward repair_limit's spend as the contract defines it; the array's positional cap still applies to both.
kind.$comment: The enumeration is asserted by GR3-15 and the requirement by GR3-09 (v3, review W-1).

repairAttempt.$comment: Hoisted at N1D so F8's positional constraint can reference it. In JSON Schema 2020-12 `items` applies ONLY to positions at or beyond len(prefixItems), so a two-entry prefixItems plus maxItems: 2 left `items` unreachable at every index a legal array can have — every constraint here was silently dead. The internal review measured it: a repair attempt of {"number": 1} alone, with no hypothesis and no result, validated. Each position now $refs this schema and adds only its own number const; `items: false` closes the tail. @3: `kind` added and required; see ADR-0037 decision 1.
